title_en: Shandong Crane Co., Ltd. v. Shandong Shanqi Heavy Industry Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of the right to enterprise name
ruling_gist_en: The abbreviation of an enterprise's name arises from the convenience of linguistic communication. The formation of an enterprise abbreviation is related to two processes: first, the enterprise itself uses the abbreviation in place of its full name; second, the public recognizes the abbreviation, i.e., acknowledges that the abbreviation and the full name refer to the same enterprise. Because the abbreviation omits certain limiting elements of the full name, it may improperly expand the scope of the objects to which the full name refers. Therefore, whether an enterprise abbreviation can specifically refer to that enterprise depends on whether the abbreviation is recognized by the relevant public and whether a stable association has been established between the abbreviation and the enterprise in the minds of the relevant public. An abbreviation of an enterprise or its name that has a certain degree of market recognition, is well-known to the relevant public, and has actually functioned as a trade name may be regarded as an enterprise name. If, through use and public recognition, a specific abbreviation of an enterprise has been recognized by the relevant public in a specific region, has corresponding market recognition, has established a stable association with that enterprise, and has the significance of a commercial identifier for identifying the business entity, and if another person subsequently uses that well-known enterprise abbreviation without authorization, which is sufficient to cause the relevant public in that specific region to confuse or mistakenly identify the subsequent user with the prior enterprise, then the subsequent user will improperly exploit the goodwill of the prior enterprise and infringe upon its lawful rights and interests. In such circumstances, the specific abbreviation of the prior enterprise shall be regarded as an enterprise name and protected in accordance with Article 5(3) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China.

full_text_en:
山东起重机有限公司与山东山起重工有限公司侵犯企业名称权纠纷案

【Ruling Summary】

The abbreviated name of an enterprise originates from the convenience of verbal communication. The formation of an enterprise's abbreviation is related to two processes: first, the enterprise itself uses the abbreviation instead of its formal name; second, the public recognizes the enterprise's abbreviation, i.e., the public accepts that the abbreviation refers to the same enterprise as its formal name. Because an abbreviation omits certain qualifying elements in the formal name, it may inappropriately expand the scope of the object referred to by the formal name. Therefore, whether an enterprise's abbreviation can specifically refer to that enterprise depends on whether the abbreviation is recognized by the relevant public and establishes a stable association with the enterprise in the minds of the relevant public. An abbreviation of an enterprise or its enterprise name that has a certain degree of market reputation, is well-known to the relevant public, and has actually functioned as a trade name may be regarded as an enterprise name. If, through use and public recognition, a specific abbreviation of an enterprise has been recognized by the relevant public in a specific region, possesses corresponding market reputation, has established a stable association with the enterprise, and has the commercial identifier significance of distinguishing business operators, then where another party subsequently uses that well-known enterprise abbreviation without authorization, which is sufficient to cause confusion or mistaken identity among the relevant public in that specific region between the subsequent user and the prior enterprise, the subsequent user will improperly exploit the goodwill of the prior enterprise and infringe the prior enterprise's lawful rights and interests. In such circumstances, the specific abbreviation of the prior enterprise shall be treated as its enterprise name and protected in accordance with Article 5, Item (3) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2008) Min Shen Zi No. 758

Applicant for Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Shandong Shanqi Heavy Industry Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 1199, Gongye Road, Qingzhou City, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Fan Xianguo, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Yuan Fazhang, male, Deputy General Manager of Shandong Shanqi Heavy Industry Co., Ltd., residing at Room 301, Unit 1, Building 61, Zone 2, No. 335, Zibo Road, Dongying District, Dongying City, Shandong Province.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Shandong Crane Factory Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 1757, Qingzhou South Road, Qingzhou City, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Xu Xinmin, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Sun Yunlong, attorney at Beijing Hetong Law Firm.

In the case concerning the dispute over infringement of enterprise name rights between the applicant for retrial, Shandong Shanqi Heavy Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shanqi Heavy Industry Company), and the respondent, Shandong Crane Factory Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shandong Crane Factory), the Shandong High People's Court rendered a civil judgment (2007) Lu Min San Zhong Zi No. 108 on June 5, 2008, which has become legally effective. On August 18, 2008, Shanqi Heavy Industry Company applied to this Court for retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to examine this case, and the examination is now concluded.

Shanqi Heavy Industry Company applied for retrial, alleging: 1. The judgments of the first and second instances contained errors in fact finding. The lawfully registered enterprise name of Shandong Crane Factory is Shandong Crane Factory Co., Ltd., which has no core trade name, nor any abbreviation or subordinate name. The trial court created a "Shanqi" trade name out of thin air through reasoning, which had not been lawfully registered. The trial court's finding that the contract for the transfer of the "Shanqi" registered trademark between Shandong Crane Factory and Shanhaiguan Crane Factory was a valid contract was inconsistent with the facts. The trial court's admission of the internal reply letter from the Individual Private Economy Supervision Division of the Shandong Administration for Industry and Commerce to the Qingzhou Administration for Industry and Commerce as valid evidence, and its use of that letter to demonstrate the legality of Shandong Crane Factory's use of the "Shanqi" abbreviation, was improper. 2. The second instance judgment incorrectly applied the law. Article 5, Item (3) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law and relevant judicial interpretations protect lawfully registered enterprise names and the trade names of well-known registered enterprise names, but do not provide protection for illogical and unregistered abbreviations of legal persons. The enterprise name of Shandong Crane Factory has no trade name at all, and the trial court's application of the above law and judicial interpretation was clearly erroneous. The name of Shanqi Heavy Industry Company was lawfully approved and registered; the company had no subjective intent to harm Shandong Crane Factory, nor did it objectively use Shandong Crane Factory's enterprise name without authorization. Therefore, its conduct did not constitute unfair competition. The trial court's decision ordering Shanqi Heavy Industry Company to compensate Shandong Crane Factory RMB 200,000 was also erroneous.

The Respondent, Shandong Crane Factory, argued in response: The facts found by the trial court were clear and the application of law was appropriate. Shanqi Heavy Industry Company's application for retrial has no factual or legal basis and should be rejected in accordance with the law.

The Weifang Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province found at first instance: Shandong Crane Factory was established in 1968, primarily engaged in the manufacture and processing of cranes. In April 1976, it was reorganized as Yidu Crane Factory. On October 31, 1991, its name was changed to Shandong Crane Factory. On January 8, 2002, Shandong Crane Factory Co., Ltd. was established, with a business scope including the design, manufacture, installation, consulting, technical services, and sales of cranes and their accessories. Shanqi Heavy Industry Company was established on February 13, 2004, and obtained its business license as a legal person on May 24, 2004. Its business scope includes the manufacture, sale, installation, and repair of cranes, belt conveyors, and petroleum machinery equipment. During the establishment of Shanqi Heavy Industry Company, the Shandong Administration for Industry and Commerce approved its pre-approved enterprise name as Shandong Shanqi Heavy Industry Co., Ltd. on January 13, 2004. On February 26, 2004, the Qingzhou Economic and Trade Bureau issued a "Report on the Application for Protection of the Name of Shandong Crane Factory Co., Ltd." to the Shandong Administration for Industry and Commerce. The report stated: "'Shanqi' is not only an abbreviation of Shandong Crane Factory but also represents the corporate image. The registration of Shanqi Heavy Industry Company has harmed the name rights of Shandong Crane Factory and caused strong repercussions among its employees. We earnestly hope that your bureau will revoke this enterprise name." On February 20, 2004, the Qingzhou Administration for Industry and Commerce requested the Shandong Administration for Industry and Commerce to study and handle the dispute arising from the enterprise name of Shanqi Heavy Industry Company. On March 9, 2004, the Individual Private Economy Supervision Division of the Shandong Administration for Industry and Commerce issued the following opinion: "Shandong Crane Factory Co., Ltd., formerly a state-owned old enterprise, uses 'Shanqi' as its enterprise abbreviation in production, operation, and external dealings. Moreover, this enterprise has a certain degree of recognition in the same industry in our province. Since the above enterprises are both located in Qingzhou City, it is easy to cause misunderstanding in society. In accordance with relevant regulations, we request that your bureau facilitate work between the two enterprises and urge Shandong Shanqi Heavy Industry Co., Ltd. to change its enterprise name with the provincial bureau." However, Shanqi Heavy Industry Company has not yet changed its enterprise name. After the dispute arose, although the parties attempted to resolve it through the Qingzhou Administration for Industry and Commerce and the Shandong Administration for Industry and Commerce, they failed to reach agreement. According to the "Industrial Economy Monthly Report" for May 2005 issued by the Qingzhou Economic and Trade Bureau, Shanqi Heavy Industry Company's total profit from January to May 2005 was RMB 1.502 million.

It was also found: On August 28, 2003, Li Yimin and others from Shandong Crane Factory applied to the Qingzhou Administration for Industry and Commerce for pre-approval of an enterprise name. On August 28, 2003, the Qingzhou Administration for Industry and Commerce issued the (Qing) Name Pre-Approval Private Zi (2003) No. 590 Notice of Pre-Approval of Enterprise Name, approving the pre-approved name of their invested enterprise as "Qingzhou Shanqi Machinery Manufacturing Co., Ltd." The retention period of this pre-approved enterprise name ended on February 27, 2004. During the retention period, it could not be used for business activities or transferred.

On July 11, 2005, Shandong Crane Factory filed a lawsuit with the Qingzhou People's Court of Shandong Province, seeking an order for Shanqi Heavy Industry Company to immediately cease using the "Shanqi" trade name, compensation for losses of RMB 500,000, and that Shanqi Heavy Industry Company bear the litigation costs. The case was later transferred to the Weifang Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province for trial.

The court of first instance held: Shandong Crane Factory is not only recognized within the same industry but also widely known to society in terms of production and operation status, enterprise scale, marketing, honors, contributions, and other aspects. It enjoys a high reputation and has formed a consumer group. Users are easily reminded of Shandong Crane Factory when they see a name bearing the words "Shanqi." Therefore, "Shanqi" should be confirmed as an abbreviation of the enterprise name of Shandong Crane Factory. Shanqi Heavy Industry Company uses "Shanqi," the core element of the well-known enterprise name that Shandong Crane Factory had used earlier. Both parties are in the same or closely related industries, and their domiciles are both in Qingzhou City, which is sufficient to cause confusion among the relevant public. It should be determined that Shanqi Heavy Industry Company has infringed Shandong Crane Factory's right to its enterprise name and should compensate Shandong Crane Factory for the economic losses caused thereby. Since Shandong Crane Factory failed to provide evidence of Shanqi Heavy Industry Company's total profits during the infringement period, nor did it provide evidence of its own losses caused by the infringement, the court, taking into account the nature, circumstances, duration, and scope of Shanqi Heavy Industry Company's infringement, and in light of the relevant data from the "Industrial Economy Monthly Report" issued by the Qingzhou Economic and Trade Bureau, determined the amount of compensation at its discretion. On September 20, 2007, the court of first instance rendered judgment (2006) Wei Min San Chu Zi No. 26, ordering Shanqi Heavy Industry Company to go through the relevant procedures with the administrative department for industry and commerce to change its enterprise name and to cease using the two characters "Shanqi" as its trade name; ordering Shanqi Heavy Industry Company to pay Shandong Crane Factory economic losses of RMB 200,000; and dismissing Shandong Crane Factory's other claims.

Shanqi Heavy Industry Company appealed the judgment of first instance to the Shandong High People's Court, arguing: Shanqi Heavy Industry Company did not engage in unfair competition, and the court of first instance's decision to order compensation of RMB 200,000 had no legal or factual basis.

The facts found by the court of second instance were consistent with those found by the court of first instance. The court of second instance also found: The contract for the transfer of the "Shanqi" registered trademark between Shandong Crane Factory and Shanhaiguan Crane Factory was confirmed as a valid contract by the Hebei High People's Court's civil judgment (2007) Ji Min Zai Zhong Zi No. 27.

The court of second instance held: Shandong Crane Factory is a well-known enterprise in the crane industry. In a specific region, particularly in Qingzhou City, "Shanqi" has been recognized by the relevant public as referring to Shandong Crane Factory, establishing a specific connection between the two, and can be regarded as a specific abbreviation of Shandong Crane Factory. Shanqi Heavy Industry Company, without proper justification, used "Shanqi" in its enterprise name. Because it is located in the same city as Shandong Crane Factory, this causes the relevant public to confuse the two enterprises, constituting unfair competition. The court of first instance, taking into account the relevant data from the "Industrial Economy Monthly Report" for May 2005 issued by the Qingzhou Economic and Trade Bureau, and comprehensively considering the nature and circumstances of Shanqi Heavy Industry Company's infringement, determined the compensation amount of RMB 200,000 to be appropriate. On June 5, 2008, the court of second instance rendered judgment dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

Upon examination, this Court finds that the facts found by the lower courts are basically true. It is further found: In this case, the use of the name "Shanqi" falls mainly into two categories. First, Shandong Crane Factory proactively used it; second, the public or other relevant entities used "Shanqi" as a substitute for "Shandong Crane Factory."

(5) Whether the judgment at first instance correctly determined that Shanqi Heavy Industry Company's use of the trade name "Shanqi" constituted unfair competition.

Where an abbreviation of an enterprise or enterprise name has a certain degree of market recognition, is well known to the relevant public, and has actually acquired the function of a trade name, it may be regarded as an enterprise name. If, through use and public recognition, a specific abbreviation of an enterprise has become recognized by the relevant public in a specific region, possesses corresponding market recognition, has established a stable connection with that enterprise, and has generated the significance of a commercial identifier for identifying the business operator, then another person's subsequent unauthorized use of that well-known enterprise abbreviation, if sufficient to cause the relevant public in that specific region to confuse the market subjects between the later user and the earlier enterprise, thereby mistaking the goods or services provided by the later user for those provided by the earlier enterprise, resulting in market confusion, the later user will improperly exploit the goodwill of the earlier enterprise and infringe upon the legitimate rights and interests of the earlier enterprise. In such circumstances, the provisions of Article 5, Item (3) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law on the protection of enterprise names may be applied to protect the specific abbreviation of that enterprise.

Shanqi Heavy Industry Company and Shandong Crane Factory are both located in Qingzhou City, in close proximity to each other, and their business scopes are substantially identical. Given that "Shanqi" had already been recognized by the relevant public as the specific abbreviation of Shandong Crane Factory, Shanqi Heavy Industry Company should have known that "Shanqi" was the specific abbreviation of Shandong Crane Factory. Under these circumstances, Shanqi Heavy Industry Company's continued use of "Shanqi" as a trade name in its enterprise name was sufficient to cause the relevant public to mistake the two enterprises, thereby infringing upon the legitimate rights and interests of Shandong Crane Factory and constituting unfair competition. Shandong Crane Factory submitted certifications from Weifang Storage and Transportation Co., Ltd., Qingzhou City Postal Bureau, and others, explaining that the relevant public had on occasion mistaken Shanqi Heavy Industry Company for Shandong Crane Factory. Although Shanqi Heavy Industry Company submitted 17 customer unit certifications, promotional materials, and photographs, these pieces of evidence can neither negate the occurrence of actual mistaken identity nor, more fundamentally, rule out the substantial likelihood of such mistaken identity. Shanqi Heavy Industry Company's claim that it did not constitute unfair competition cannot be sustained, and this court does not uphold it.

(6) Whether the judgment at first instance correctly ordered Shanqi Heavy Industry Company to pay RMB 200,000 in damages to Shandong Crane Factory.

Given that the profits gained by Shanqi Heavy Industry Company from the infringement and the losses suffered by Shandong Crane Factory could not be ascertained, the court at first instance, taking into comprehensive consideration the nature, circumstances, duration, and scope of the infringing acts of Shanqi Heavy Industry Company, and in light of relevant data from the "Industrial Economic Monthly Report" issued by the Qingzhou City Economic and Trade Bureau, determined a damages amount of RMB 200,000 at its discretion. This determination was not improper.

In conclusion, the retrial application of Shanqi Heavy Industry Company does not satisfy the requirements of Article 179 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 181, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows:

The retrial application of Shandong Shanqi Heavy Industry Co., Ltd. is hereby dismissed.

Presiding Judge: Wang Yongchang

Judge: He Zhonglin

Acting Judge: Li Jian

April 27, 2009

Clerk: Wang Xin
